title: Saptajana hermitage
introduction: After encouraging Sugreeva to challenge Vali for a second time duly wearing a flower garland as a mark of identification between the two brothers, Rama and others proceed to Kishkindha. On their way they chance to see a divine hermitage called sapta jana aashrama 'Hermitage of Seven Sages.' On worshipping it they proceed to Kishkindha.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये किष्किन्ध काण्डे त्रयोदशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 13th chapter in Kishkindha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
ऋश्यमूकात् स धर्मात्मा किष्किन्धाम् लक्ष्मण अग्रजः |
जगाम सह सुग्रीवो वालि विक्रम पालिताम्
समुद्यम्य महत् चापम् रामः कांचन भूषितम् |
शराम् च आदित्य संकाशान् गृहीत्वा रण साधकान्
verses.iast:
ṛśyamūkāt sa dharmātmā kiṣkindhām lakṣmaṇa agrajaḥ |
jagāma saha sugrīvo vāli vikrama pālitām
samudyamya mahat cāpam rāmaḥ kāṃcana bhūṣitam |
śarām ca āditya saṅkāśān gṛhītvā raṇa sādhakān
verses.translation: That righteous Rama readying his great bow decorated with gold, and on taking blazing sun similar arrows that are victory-oriented in wars, proceeded from Rishyamuka along with Sugreeva to the city ruled by the valour of Vali, namely Kishkindha.

verses.devanagari:
अग्रतः तु ययौ तस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः |
सुग्रीवः संहत ग्रीवो लक्ष्मणः च महाबलः
verses.iast:
agrataḥ tu yayau tasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ |
sugrīvaḥ saṃhata grīvo lakṣmaṇaḥ ca mahābalaḥ
verses.translation: Stern-necked Sugreeva and the great mighty Lakshmana strode ahead of that great soul Rama.

verses.devanagari:
पृष्ठतो हनुमान् वीरो नलो नीलः च वीर्यवान् |
तारः चैव महातेजा हरि यूथप यूथपाः
verses.iast:
pṛṣṭhato hanumān vīro nalo nīlaḥ ca vīryavān |
tāraḥ caiva mahātejā hari yūthapa yūthapāḥ
verses.translation: The brave Hanuma, dauntless Nala and Neela, and the captain of monkey's captains Tara of great energy followed them rearward.

glosses.meaning: of great energy, monkeys, captain of, captains Tara. [yayau = proceeded.]

verses.devanagari:
ते वीक्षमाणा वृक्षाम् च पुष्प भार अवलम्बिनः |
प्रसन्न अंबुवहाः चैव सरितः सागरम् गमाः
verses.iast:
te vīkṣamāṇā vṛkṣām ca puṣpa bhāra avalambinaḥ |
prasanna ambuvahāḥ caiva saritaḥ sāgaram gamāḥ
verses.translation: They moved on looking at the trees that are drooping with the weight of their flowers, and at he rivers that are carrying pleasant water while themselves are coursing towards ocean.

verses.devanagari:
कन्दराणि च शैलाम् च निर्दराणि गुहाः तथा |
शिखराणि च मुख्यानि दरीः च प्रिय दर्शनाः
verses.iast:
kandarāṇi ca śailām ca nirdarāṇi guhāḥ tathā |
śikharāṇi ca mukhyāni darīḥ ca priya darśanāḥ
verses.translation: They on seeing house-like caverns, crags, ravines and caves, and monumental peaks, cavities that are pleasant for sight have moved on.
notes: The words kandara, and guha have different meanings. kandarāṇi = mandira ākāra parvata vivarāṇi =house-like mountain cavities; nir+darāṇi = śaila vivarāṇi; guhāḥ = deva khāta giri bilvāni-deep mountain caves made by divinities - Rama Tilaka.

verses.devanagari:
वैदूर्य विमलैः तोयैः पद्मैः च आकोश कुड्मलैः |
शोभितान् सजलान् मार्गे तटाकान् च अवलोकयन्
verses.iast:
vaidūrya vimalaiḥ toyaiḥ padmaiḥ ca ākośa kuḍmalaiḥ |
śobhitān sajalān mārge taṭākān ca avalokayan
verses.translation: On their way they observed lakes that are glistening forth with gem-like waters without slime, and with lotus buds in budding stage.
notes: The word ākośakuḍmalaiḥ has other renderings. One is as above, saying the lotuses in lakes are still in the budding stage and they have not started to bloom. The other is that they are neither large not tiny in size. Another is that the stem is having all buds from below to its end, if the compound is separated as ā kośa kuḍmalaiḥ .

Secondly the usage of vaidūrya vimala udaka is an often-repeated expression, which may not be construed that the waters are just like cats-eye or Lapis Lazule, the precocious gem in nava ratna / nine-gem combination. In fine composition it is smaraṇa alankāra , a metaphorical memorabilia. If it is said that the water is like vaidūrya or cat's-eye or Lapis, it reminds us of all other eight gems including a diamond. As such the waters are crystalline and pellucid in their look like priceless gems, for water is the invaluable gem-like gift of nature and flowing waters are the priceless possessions for livelihood as well.

The following two verses contain the foots in one samāsa/ one compound which if read in a spell will be rhythmic. The first foot of verse nine is one samāsa / one compound only. Both the unbroken compound and segregated word order are given below for reading pleasure.

verses.devanagari:
कारण्डैस्सारसैर्हंसैर्वञ्जुलैर्जलकुक्कुटैः |
चक्रवाकैस्थाचान्यैश्शकुनैर्प्रतिनादितान् || - यद्वा -
कारण्डैः सारसैः हंसैः वंजुलैः जल कुक्कुटैः |
चक्रवाकैः तथा च अन्यैः शकुनैः प्रतिनादितान्
verses.iast:
kāraṇḍaissārasai.rhaṃsai.rvañjulai.rjalakukkuṭaiḥ |
cakravākaisthācānyaiśśakunai.rpratināditān || - yadvā -
kāraṇḍaiḥ sārasaiḥ haṃsaiḥ vaṃjulaiḥ jala kukkuṭaiḥ |
cakravākaiḥ tathā ca anyaiḥ śakunaiḥ pratināditān
verses.translation: Those lakes are reverberant with Karandava-s, Saarasa-s, Swans, Vanjula-s and other waterfowls, also like that with Chakravaaka-s and other birds.

glosses.itrans: kaaraNDaiH saarasaiH hamsaiH vanjulaiH jala kukkuTaiH
glosses.iast: kāraṇḍaiḥ sārasaiḥ hamsaiḥ vanjulaiḥ jala kukkuṭaiḥ
glosses.devanagari: कारण्डैः सारसैः हम्सैः वन्जुलैः जल कुक्कुटैः
glosses.meaning: Karandava, Saarasa, Swans, Vanjula water, fowls

verses.devanagari:
मृदुशष्पाङ्कुराअहारान्निर्भयान्वनगोचरान् |
चरतांसर्वतोपश्यन्स्थलीषु हरिणान्स्थितान् || - यद्वा -
मृदु शष्प अंकुर आहारान् निर्भयान् वन गोचरान् |
चरताम् सर्वतो अपश्यन् स्थलीषु हरिणान् स्थितान्
verses.iast:
mṛduśaṣpāñkurāahārānnirbhayānvanagocarān |
caratāṃsarvatopaśyansthalīṣu hariṇānsthitān || - yadvā -
mṛdu śaṣpa aṃkura āhārān nirbhayān vana gocarān |
caratām sarvato apaśyan sthalīṣu hariṇān sthitān
verses.translation: They have seen fearless deer feeding on soft grass blades everywhere, somewhere moving here and there in the forest, and else where standing.

verses.devanagari:
तटाक वैरिणः च अपि शुक्ल दन्त विभूषितान् |
घोरान् एकचरान् वन्यान् द्विरदान् कूल घातिनः
verses.iast:
taṭāka vairiṇaḥ ca api śukla danta vibhūṣitān |
ghorān ekacarān vanyān dviradān kūla ghātinaḥ
verses.translation: They have also seen the forest elephants that have white tusks for their ornaments and that are moving in herds, and which are the dangerous enemies of lakes as they destroy lakebeds.

verses.devanagari:
मत्तन् गिरि तट उद्घुष्टान् पर्वतान् इव जंगमान् |
वानरान् द्विरद प्रख्यान् मही रेणु समुक्षितान्
verses.iast:
mattan giri taṭa udghuṣṭān parvatān iva jaṃgamān |
vānarān dvirada prakhyān mahī reṇu samukśitān
verses.translation: Also seen are the vigorous and elephantine monkeys that are like mobile mountains, begrimed with dust, and bellowing on mountain ridges.
notes: If the first foot mattān giri taṭa udghuṣṭān is connected with verse 10, it can also be said in respect of elephants like 'the elephants in rut are moving like mobile mountains and noisy on the mountain crags.'

verses.devanagari:
वने वन चराम् च अन्यान् खेचराम् च विहंगमान् |
पश्यन्तः त्वरिता जग्मुः सुग्रीव वश वर्तिनः
verses.iast:
vane vana carām ca anyān khecarām ca vihaṅgamān |
paśyantaḥ tvaritā jagmuḥ sugrīva vaśa vartinaḥ
verses.translation: On seeing other forest beings in that forest and birds moving aloft in sky, those followers of Sugreeva quickly moved on.
notes: The two words vihangama and khecara mean a bird. But the vihangama is the cognate word and khecara is its adjective, as observed by Dr. Satya Vrat in his: The Ramayana - A Linguist Study.

glosses.meaning: Sugreeva's, under control, that move - followers of Sugreeva

verses.devanagari:
तेषाम् तु गच्छताम् तत्र त्वरितम् रघुनंदनः |
द्रुम षण्ड वनम् दृष्ट्वा रामः सुग्रीवम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
teṣām tu gacchatām tatra tvaritam raghunaṃdanaḥ |
druma ṣaṇḍa vanam dṛṣṭvā rāmaḥ sugrīvam abravīt
verses.translation: While they are quickly going, Rama, the delight of Raghu's dynasty, saw there a clump of forest trees and he asked Sugreeva like this.

verses.devanagari:
एष मेघ इव आकाशे वृक्ष षण्डः प्रकाशते |
मेघ संघात विपुलः पर्यन्त कदली वृतः
verses.iast:
eṣa megha iva ākāśe vṛkṣa ṣaṇḍaḥ prakāśate |
megha saṃghāta vipulaḥ paryanta kadalī vṛtaḥ
verses.translation: "This cluster of trees surrounded with plantain trees is like an accumulation of thick clouds, and this is shining forth like a cloudscape in sky.

glosses.meaning: in sky, cloud [cloudscape,] like, shining forth.

verses.devanagari:
किम् एतत् ज्ञातुम् इच्छामि सखे कौतूहलम् मम |
कौतूहल अपनयनम् कर्तुम् इच्छामि अहम् त्वया
verses.iast:
kim etat jñātum icchāmi sakhe kautūhalam mama |
kautūhala apanayanam kartum icchāmi aham tvayā
verses.translation: "What is this? I wish to know and oh, friend, I wish you to clear this inquisitiveness of mine.

glosses.itrans: kautuuhala apanayanam kartum aham icChaami tvayaa
glosses.iast: kautūhala apanayanam kartum aham icchāmi tvayā
glosses.devanagari: कौतूहल अपनयनं कर्तुं अहं इच्छामि त्वया
glosses.meaning: inquisitiveness, to be clear, be made, I, wish to, by you.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य तद् वचनम् श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः |
गच्छन्न् एव आचचक्षे अथ सुग्रीवः तत् महद् वनम्
verses.iast:
tasya tad vacanam śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ |
gacchann eva ācacakṣe atha sugrīvaḥ tat mahad vanam
verses.translation: On hearing that sentence of that great soul Raghava, then Sugreeva described about the significance of that forest while proceeding on the way.

verses.devanagari:
एतद् राघव विस्तीर्णम् आश्रमम् श्रम नाशनम् |
उद्यान वन संपन्नम् स्वादु मूल फल उदकम्
verses.iast:
etad rāghava vistīrṇam āśramam śrama nāśanam |
udyāna vana sampannam svādu mūla phala udakam
verses.translation: "Raghava, this spacious hermitage with abundant gardens and dainty tubers, fruits and water is a weary remover." Thus Sugreeva started telling Rama.

verses.devanagari:
अत्र सप्तजना नाम मुनयः संशित व्रताः |
सप्त एव आसन् अधः शीर्षा नियतम् जल शायिनः
verses.iast:
atra saptajanā nāma munayaḥ saṃśita vratāḥ |
sapta eva āsan adhaḥ śīrṣā niyatam jala śāyinaḥ
verses.translation: "There were hermits named sapta jana, Seven Persons, who were dourly vowed with their heads pendulous downward and legs up, as in shiirSa aasana , the upside-down yogic body posture, and who always reclined in water.

verses.devanagari:
सप्त रात्रे कृत आहारा वायुना अचल वासिनः |
दिवम् वर्ष शतैः याताः सप्तभिः सकलेवराः
verses.iast:
sapta rātre kṛta āhārā vāyunā acala vāsinaḥ |
divam varṣa śataiḥ yātāḥ saptabhiḥ sakalevarāḥ
verses.translation: "They were making diet on air alone that too once in seven days, and living unwaveringly in that way they practised their asceticism for seven hundred years and went to heavens with their bodies.

glosses.meaning: seven years, hundred - for seven hundred years [of their ascesis]
with, bodies, to heaven, they went.

verses.devanagari:
तेषाम् एतत् प्रभावेण द्रुम प्राकार संवृतम् |
आश्रमम् सुदुराधर्षम् अपि स इन्द्रैः सुर असुरैः
verses.iast:
teṣām etat prabhāveṇa druma prākāra saṃvṛtam |
āśramam sudurādharṣam api sa indraiḥ sura asuraiḥ
verses.translation: "This hermitage that has encircling trees for its compound wall has become highly unassailable even for Indra together with all gods and demons.

glosses.meaning: with, Indra, by gods, by demons, even

verses.devanagari:
पक्षिणो वर्जयन्ति एतत् तथा अन्ये वनचारिणः |
विशन्ति मोहाद् ये अपि अत्र न निवर्तन्ते ते पुनः
verses.iast:
pakṣiṇo varjayanti etat tathā anye vanacāriṇaḥ |
viśanti mohād ye api atra na nivartante te punaḥ
verses.translation: "Birds and other forest moving animals forbear this hermitage and those that unknowingly enter in there they do not return.

verses.devanagari:
विभूषण रवाअः च अत्र श्रूयंते सकलाक्षराः |
तूर्य गीत स्वनाअः च अपि गन्धो दिव्यः च राघव
verses.iast:
vibhūṣaṇa ravāaḥ ca atra śrūyaṃte sakalākṣarāḥ |
tūrya gīta svanāaḥ ca api gandho divyaḥ ca rāghava
verses.translation: "From there artistically worded lyrical and instrumental tunes, and even the sounds of ornaments are audible, and oh, Raghava, one can sense a divine fragrance too.

glosses.meaning: sa kala akSaraaH = with, artistically, worded
ca fragrance, divine, also - you can smell.

verses.devanagari:
त्रेताग्नयो अपि दीप्यन्ते धूमो हि एष प्रदृश्यते |
वेष्टयन् इव वृक्ष अग्रान् कपोत अंग अरुणो घनः
verses.iast:
tretāgnayo api dīpyante dhūmo hi eṣa pradṛśyate |
veṣṭayan iva vṛkṣa agrān kapota aṃga aruṇo ghanaḥ
verses.translation: "Even the triadic ritual-fires glow there, and their thick and ochry coloured smoke like that of a reddish-brown pigeon is apparent muffling the treetops.

glosses.meaning: pigeon, body's, ochre-coloured [unlike those of white or grey Columba livia species]

verses.devanagari:
एते वृक्षाः प्रकाशन्ते धूम संसक्त मस्तकाः |
मेघ जाल प्रतिच्छन्ना वैदूर्य गिरयो यथा
verses.iast:
ete vṛkśāḥ prakāśante dhūma saṃsak{}ta mastakāḥ |
megha jāla praticchannā vaidūrya girayo yathā
verses.translation: "When that smoke is mantling their tops these trees are beaming forth like mountains of gems overlaid with clusters of clouds.

glosses.meaning: smoke, mantled, with heads - at treetops

verses.devanagari:
कुरु प्रणामम् धर्मात्मन् तेषाम् उद्दिश्य राघवः |
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा प्रयतः संयत अंजलिः
verses.iast:
kuru praṇāmam dharmātman teṣām uddiśya rāghavaḥ |
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā prayataḥ saṃyata aṃjaliḥ
verses.translation: "Offer salutations determinedly and adjoining palms addressing the sages called Seven Persons, oh Raghava, along with brother Lakshmana

verses.devanagari:
प्रणमन्ति हि ये तेषाम् ऋषीणाम् भावित आत्मनाम् |
न तेषाम् अशुभम् किंचित् शरीरे राम दृश्यते
verses.iast:
praṇamanti hi ye teṣām ṛṣīṇām bhāvita ātmanām |
na teṣām aśubham kiñcit śarīre rāma dṛśyate
verses.translation: "Those that offer salutations to those sages with contemplated souls will evince no bodily trauma in the least." Thus said Sugreeva to Rama.

glosses.meaning: contemplated souls, at them, those sages

verses.devanagari:
ततो रामः सह भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणेन कृतांजलिः |
समुद्दिश्य महात्मानः तान् ऋषीन् अभ्यवादयत्
verses.iast:
tato rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena kṛtāṃjaliḥ |
samuddiśya mahātmānaḥ tān ṛṣīn abhyavādayat
verses.translation: Then Rama along with brother Lakshmana adjoined palms, addressed himself to the great-souled sages known as Seven Persons, and offered salutations to them.

glosses.meaning: great souled ones, them the sages, on addressing

verses.devanagari:
अभिवाद्य च धर्मात्मा रामो भ्राता च लक्ष्मणः |
सुग्रीवो वानराअः चैव जग्मुः संहृष्ट मानसाः |
verses.iast:
abhivādya ca dharmātmā rāmo bhrātā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ |
sugrīvo vānarāaḥ caiva jagmuḥ saṃhṛṣṭa mānasāḥ |
verses.translation: That righteous Rama along with brother Lakshmana, Sugreeva and other monkeys having worshipped those sages proceeded to Kishkindha well-pleased at heart.

glosses.itrans: raamaH bhraataa lakSmaNaH sugriivaH vaanaraaaH caiva
glosses.iast: rāmaḥ bhrātā lakṣmaṇaḥ sugrīvaḥ vānarāaḥ caiva
glosses.devanagari: रामः भ्राता लक्ष्मणः सुग्रीवः वानराअः चैव
glosses.meaning: Rama, brother, Lakshmana, Sugreeva, monkeys, also thus

verses.devanagari:
ते गत्वा दूरम् अध्वानम् तस्मात् सप्त जन आश्रमात् |
ददृशुः ताम् दुराधर्षाम् किष्किन्धाम् वालि पालिताम्
verses.iast:
te gatvā dūram adhvānam tasmāt sapta jana āśramāt |
dadṛśuḥ tām durādharṣām kiṣkindhām vāli pālitām
verses.translation: Having gone a long way from that hermitage of Seven Persons they have seen that unassailable and Vali ruled city namely Kishkindha.

glosses.itrans: vaali paalitaam duraadharSaam taam kiSkindhaam dadR^ishuH
glosses.iast: vāli pālitām durādharṣām tām kiṣkindhām dadṛśuḥ
glosses.devanagari: वालि पालितां दुराधर्षां तां किष्किन्धां ददृशुः
glosses.meaning: by Vali, ruled, unassailable one, her, that Kishkindha, they saw.

verses.devanagari:
ततस्तु रामानुज राम वानराः
प्रगृह्य शस्त्राणि उदित उग्र तेजसा |
पुरीम् सुरेश आत्मज वीर्य पालिताम्
वधाय शत्रोः पुनर् आगताः इह
verses.iast:
tatastu rāmānuja rāma vānarāḥ
pragṛhya śastrāṇi udita ugra tejasā |
purīm sureśa ātmaja vīrya pālitām
vadhāya śatroḥ punar āgatāḥ iha
verses.translation: Then Rama's bother Lakshmana, Rama, and other monkeys wielding their weapons and flaring with their upsurged fiery again came to eliminate that enemy Vali to the city that is ruled by the brawn of the same Vali, the son of Indra.

glosses.meaning: up surged, fiery, with flare of
